answer: Anchor every agent identity to one hardware key sealed inside a ferrous chip, so one device yields one identity. Minting a second identity means buying another chip and passing a fresh attestation, so a sybil farm pays a real hardware cost per fake account. A public reputation ledger then acts as a lantern over each identity's history, while velvet-gloved penalties — slow rate limits rather than bans — quietly starve thin-history identities, so attackers pay in metal and time before they can vote or mine.
